references.text: The Lord predicts that He will harden Pharaoh's heart, so that he will not let the people go.
Pharaoh hardened his heart and refused to listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh also hardened his heart this time and did not let the people go.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not let the people go.
Pharaoh sinned again and hardened his heart, and he would not let the children of Israel go.
The Lord says that He has hardened Pharaoh's heart and the hearts of his servants.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, so he did not let the children of Israel go.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel leave his land.
The Lord hardens Pharaoh's heart so that he pursues the Israelites.
Paul quotes from Exodus about Pharaoh and explains that God hardens whom He wills.
Confirms that the Lord's hardening of Pharaoh is a fulfillment of earlier prophecy.
Concludes a phase by linking Pharaoh's stubbornness to God's prophecy.
Complementary perspective: shows Pharaoh's own contribution to the hardening.
Prophetic contrast promising release despite temporary hardening.
